title: PACELC Theorem
description: Learn how PACELC extends CAP to describe trade-offs even when no partition occurs.

data.text: CAP answers a narrow question: what happens during a partition? PACELC, introduced by Daniel Abadi, broadens the lens. It states that in a distributed system, even when there is no partition, there is a trade-off between latency and consistency. The acronym breaks down as: Partition: choose between Availability and Consistency; Else: choose between Latency and Consistency. This captures the reality that strong consistency often requires coordination that adds round-trip time.

When a system replicates data across regions, synchronous replication keeps all replicas identical but increases write latency because the leader must wait for acknowledgments from followers. Asynchronous replication reduces latency because the leader returns immediately, but followers may lag, violating read-your-writes consistency. PACELC gives you vocabulary to describe why a system designer chose synchronous replication for financial records and asynchronous replication for activity feeds.

data.caption: PACELC trade-offs: two decision points for a distributed system.

flowchart TD
    Start[Distributed System] --> Partition{Partition?}
    Partition -->|Yes| PA[P: Availability vs Consistency]
    Partition -->|No| EL[E: Latency vs Consistency]
    PA --> PA_AV[Choose Availability: return stale data]
    PA --> PA_C[Choose Consistency: reject requests or wait]
    EL --> EL_L[Choose Latency: serve local replica]
    EL --> EL_C[Choose Consistency: sync across replicas]
    PA_AV --> End[Trade-off decided]
    PA_C --> End
    EL_L --> End
    EL_C --> End

data.title: Interview Tip
data.text: Mentioning PACELC in a system design interview signals that you understand consistency is not just a partition-time concern. It shows you think about latency and user experience continuously.

terms.definition: A replication mode where the leader waits for acknowledgments from followers before confirming a write.
A replication mode where the leader confirms writes immediately and followers catch up later.
A guarantee that a user can read their own writes after they complete.

items.question: Does PACELC replace CAP?
items.answer: No. PACELC extends CAP by covering the else case. Use both: CAP for partition-time behavior and PACELC for everyday latency trade-offs.

items.question: Is every system PACELC?
items.answer: Most replicated systems are. Single-node systems are not distributed, so the theorem does not apply.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: PACELC adds latency to the consistency conversation.
Synchronous replication improves consistency at the cost of latency.
Asynchronous replication improves latency at the cost of temporary inconsistency.
Use PACELC when you need to explain replication or geo-distribution choices.
data.takeaway: PACELC reveals that consistency trade-offs happen every day, not just during partitions.
